args.summary: The v2.3.1 deployment of checkout-api caused failing health checks and elevated error rates (0.18) in production. Per the runbook, we rolled back all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to the most recent previously healthy release, v2.3.0. The initial rollback partially failed in us-east, so a second rollback was executed to complete the rollout. Service is now healthy in all regions on v2.3.0 with error rate at 0.002. v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed until root cause is investigated.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened:

1. **Diagnosed**: The latest deploy, **v2.3.1**, was unhealthy in production, while **v2.3.0** was the most recent release that had been healthy in production.
2. **Rolled back** checkout-api to v2.3.0. The first attempt only completed in us-east (orchestrator error), so I retried — the second rollback succeeded in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west).
3. **Verified recovery**: All regions are now on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate dropped from 0.18 back to 0.002.
4. **Opened incident** **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api, describing the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the partial-then-completed rollback, and current healthy state; the on-call engineer has been paged. The first incident-creation call timed out, but thanks to the idempotency key, the retry did not create a duplicate (confirmed via the incident list).

Recommendation: hold off redeploying v2.3.1 until root cause of the health check failures is investigated.

All three regions are now on v2.3.0 and healthy again (error rate back to 0.2%). Now I'll open the SEV2 incident.
